about: The frozen byte-identity corpus of the Rust port (the port plan's phase 0b): places whose plans, cell facts, road and far tiles, terrain blocks and messages every port step must leave byte-identical. Each place: its point, why it is in the corpus, plan_half_m (the box round the point whose map cells build.py plans and makes the facts of), and the session's view (session.py: viewM, the far field's reach the graphics message asks, and seconds of posing after far_done). Change this file only together with a new corpus folder: the stored 'before' outputs are of these exact boxes.

fells_point.why: the test city: rowhouse streets, Thames Street's cobbles, piers and the harbour (sea), parking, sidewalks, traffic signals

manhattan_penn.why: Penn Station / Midtown: the densest roads, buildings and rail (tunnels under the station, the High Line's decks), the cold-NYC benchmark

vienna_s1_rautenweg.why: S1 under Rautenweg: an underpass the DEM shows open, grade separations, level ranges across glibc versions (FACTS_FORMAT 17 / 19)

stelvio.why: the Stelvio pass: switchbacks (Spec.mountain), steep grading, parapets, high relief

phoenix_i10.why: I-10 in Phoenix: a motorway with ramps, stack interchanges and medians, desert flat ground (the high-speed runs' road)

zermatt.why: an Alpine town in a deep valley: tunnels, rail, steep relief, European road rules

tromso.why: 69.6 N: a high-latitude frame (cells shrink with cos(lat)), sea, a long bridge and road tunnels, Nordic rules

laramie.why: a small high-plains town: a grid of streets, the rail yard and its crossings, sparse buildings, gravel roads
